protocol.split: first third training; second third calibration; final third held out
protocol.shift_timing: shift begins halfway through held-out period; training and calibration remain unchanged
protocol.generator: factor marginals stay standard-normal while correlation changes from +0.82 to -0.82
protocol.evidence_scope: The lens cites a cross-entity factor window. This report scores event detection, not the framework's same-entity evidence-integrity metric.
protocol.label_policy: all held-out events from the change point onward are labeled as belonging to the changed regime
protocol.evaluation_unit: exact event IDs in the held-out period
protocol.selection_rule: candidate families and thresholds were specified before held-out scoring; only training and calibration data determine fitted values and thresholds
protocol.external_validation: See the existing NAB real-series reports; NAB labels are public window annotations, not independent expert adjudication, and the task differs from correlation-regime detection.

limitations: This is a controlled synthetic test, not evidence on FX transactions or real market regimes.
The benchmark evaluates known candidate lenses; it does not prove that an automated lens selector will choose correctly on unseen domains.
The shifted regime occupies only half of each held-out period; the unchanged half provides a held-out false-positive check.
The external NAB results use independently published anomaly windows, but no blind expert adjudication was performed and the data are univariate time series.
Correlation evidence is cohort-wide. The current entity-local evidence-integrity check is not a suitable quality measure for these references and is not reported here.
A/B/D/E agent runs remain unavailable; this experiment does not establish REFLEX superiority over a general-purpose agent.
